Term 1 · Spotting AI in the Wild

Weeks 1–9

What is AI really, and what is it made of?

WEEK 01📘 teach

Is It Smart, or Is It Just Following Orders?

AI is a machine doing a job that used to need a person's judgement — not a brain, not magic.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 02📘 teach

The Machine That Learns the Rule By Itself

In machine learning nobody writes the rule; the machine finds it by studying labelled examples.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 03🔬 lab

AI Detective: Find 15 in Your Own Day

Almost every AI you meet is narrow — brilliant at one job, blank at everything else.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 04📘 teach

Everything a Machine Knows Arrived as a Table

Whatever an AI knows arrived as rows and columns — one row is one thing, one column is one measurement.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 05📘 teach

Numbers, Names, and Broken Boxes

Every column has a type, and the four kinds of mess — missing, duplicate, impossible, typo — are findable if you look.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 06🔬 lab

Where Did This Data Come From?

Thirty rows about you are a sample, not the world — and a data card is how you stay honest about that.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 07📘 teach

Patterns: Things That Repeat Enough to Bet On

A pattern repeats often enough that betting on it beats guessing; a rule is a pattern written down for a computer.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 08📘 teach

Where Rules Break: Edge Cases and False Alarms

Every rule has edge cases, and the two ways to be wrong — false alarms and misses — hurt different people.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 09🔁 review

Term 1 Checkpoint — Rules on Trial

A rulebook scored on the messages you wrote it from tells you nothing; the honest score is on messages it has never seen.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script

Term 2 · Teaching a Machine to Guess

Weeks 10–18

How do you turn the world into examples a machine can learn from?

WEEK 10🛠️ project

The Rule Explosion: Why Nobody Writes 258 Rules

Adding rules to cover exceptions grows faster than the exceptions do — that wall is why machine learning was invented.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 11📘 teach

How a Machine Describes Your Dog

A feature is one measured description of one example; the label is the answer you want back.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 12📘 teach

Useful, Useless, and Sneaky Features

A feature is only useful if it beats guessing — and a leaky feature already contains the answer.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 13📘 teach

Which One? or How Much?

Classification picks from a short list; regression predicts a number — the same table does either, depending on which column you cover.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 14🔬 lab

Feature Card Deck: Make a Human Be the Model

If your features are good enough, a stranger who has never seen the thing can guess its label from the numbers alone.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 15📘 teach

Training: Turning 120 Photos Into a Guessing Machine

Training reads labelled examples once and produces a model; after that the examples are gone and only the model remains.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 16📘 teach

Confidence Is Not Correctness

A confidence score is guess strength, not a promise, and the margin tells you how close the race was.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 17🔬 lab

Train Your First Real Model

You can build a working image classifier in twenty minutes without code — and it will be exactly as good as the photos you gave it.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 18🔁 review

Term 2 Checkpoint — Break Your Own Model on Purpose

Change one thing at a time and the model will tell you exactly what it was relying on.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script

Term 3 · Trust, Proof, and Pixels

Weeks 19–27

How do you prove a model is any good — and what is it looking at?

WEEK 19📘 teach

The Test You Can't Study For

Testing a model on the examples it trained on is cheating; you must hide examples before training and never let it see them.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 20📘 teach

Accuracy, Three Ways — and the Number That Lies

Accuracy is correct ÷ total, and one accuracy number can hide a class that is completely broken.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 21📘 teach

Memorizing vs Generalizing

A model scoring 100% on its own photos and 40% on new ones didn't learn the object — it learned the photos.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 22🛠️ project

The Hidden Ten: Test Your Own Model Honestly

The only number worth reporting is the one you got on examples the model had never seen.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 23📘 teach

A Photo Is Just a Grid of Numbers

To a computer a picture is nothing but a grid of brightness numbers from 0 to 255.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 24📘 teach

Colour Is Three Grids Stacked

A colour picture is three number grids — red, green, blue — and shrinking an image throws information away forever.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 25📘 teach

Filters: The Little Grid That Finds Edges

Slide a tiny grid of numbers over an image and it highlights one thing; an edge is a sudden change in brightness.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 26🔬 lab

Pixel Lab: Make the Outline Appear

Edges survive a change of lighting and raw brightness does not — that is why vision models look for edges first.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 27🔁 review

Term 3 Checkpoint — From Pixels to Words

Everything a machine handles first becomes numbers in a table; text is no different from a photo.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script

Term 4 · Words, Fairness, and Your Own AI

Weeks 28–36

How do machines handle language, who does AI let down, and can you build one and defend it honestly?

WEEK 28📘 teach

Counting Word Pairs: The Whole Engine

A language model is a giant tally of which word tends to follow which — nothing more mysterious than that.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 29📘 teach

Dice, Fluency, and Making Things Up

Randomness is why the same prompt gives different answers — and a sentence can be perfectly fluent and completely false.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 30🔬 lab

Build a Chatbot in Scratch

A rule-based bot and a learned language model fail in completely different ways, and knowing which you're talking to changes your trust.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 31📘 teach

Who Is Missing From the Photos?

Bias is not the machine being mean — it is a gap in who was in the training data, showing up as a gap in accuracy.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 32📘 teach

Your Data, Fakes, and Trusting Too Much

A photo carries more than a picture, a confident answer is not a correct one, and something real-looking can be made in ten minutes.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 33🔬 lab

Audit Your Own Model

The most trustworthy thing you can do with your own model is show, with numbers, the group it fails on.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 34🎪 capstone

The AI Fair Booth, Part 1: Build It and Test It Honestly

A real AI project is not the model — it is the model plus the honest paperwork saying what it can and cannot do.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 35🎪 capstone

The AI Fair Booth, Part 2: The App, the Report, the Demo

If you can show your model failing and explain why, you understand it — anyone can show it working.

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
WEEK 36🏁 assessment

Showcase Day: Prove It, Present It, Celebrate It

You can build a guessing machine, measure it honestly, find who it fails, and explain all of it without saying "magic".

📗 Chapter✏️ Workbook🧑‍🏫 Lesson script
